variants.title: Resistance of a wire: nichrome, SWG 26
variants.note: A thinner wire of the same material: the area falls to two thirds, so the resistance of the same length rises by half.

source.title: Published resistivity of Ni80Cr20 nichrome at 20 C, 1.09e-6 ohm m; SWG 26 diameter 0.4572 mm (BS 3737 standard wire gauge)

variants.title: Resistance of a wire: constantan, SWG 24
variants.note: The same length and the same thickness as the nichrome wire, but a different material: the resistance is less than half.

source.title: Kaye & Laby, Tables of Physical and Chemical Constants: resistivity of constantan (Cu55Ni45) at 20 C, 4.9e-7 ohm m; SWG 24 diameter 0.5588 mm (BS 3737)

variants.title: Resistance of a wire: manganin, SWG 24
variants.note: Manganin is used for standard resistance coils because its resistance hardly changes with temperature.

source.title: Kaye & Laby, Tables of Physical and Chemical Constants: resistivity of manganin at 20 C, 4.82e-7 ohm m; SWG 24 diameter 0.5588 mm (BS 3737)

variants.title: Resistance of a wire: iron, SWG 22
variants.note: A thicker wire of a far better conductor: the same length has about a fortieth of the nichrome wire's resistance.

source.title: Kaye & Laby, Tables of Physical and Chemical Constants: electrical resistivity of iron at 20 C, 9.71e-8 ohm m; SWG 22 diameter 0.7112 mm (BS 3737)
